1.explanation: At import time the TreeWalker walks boundary events specially, pushing the boundary event onto the deferred queue so it is drawn early, but then invokes dataInputAssociations and dataOutputAssociations immediately (synchronously) rather than deferring them. Because those associations are handled before the boundary event shape exists in the element registry, the importer (_getSource/_getTarget) cannot find the boundary event element and thus silently fails to create the DataAssociation connection. By moving the handleDataAssociation calls for boundary events into the deferred queue (just like other flow node associations), the DataAssociation will be drawn after the boundary event has been created and the missing dotted line will appear.
1.bug_scenario: The user models a BPMN diagram in the online editor by attaching a signal boundary event to a task and then creating a data‐object association from that boundary event to a data object (shown as a dotted line). After exporting the BPMN XML, refreshing the page and re‐importing that file, the boundary event is still drawn correctly but the data association (the dotted arrow to the data object) is completely missing.
